sections.1.heading: Windows time tracking software without an installer
sections.1.body:
Many people searching for **Windows time tracking software** expect to download a program. Paidlyo works differently: it runs in the web browser you already use on Windows. There's no installer, nothing for IT to approve, and no updates to manage.

That's a deliberate choice, with real trade-offs, and this page covers both sides. The short version:

- **You get** the same timer, weekly timesheet, reports and invoices on every PC you sign in from, with all your team's hours in one shared account.
- **You don't get** the things a desktop program can do in the background, such as tracking which apps you use, detecting idle time or working offline.

Paidlyo is built for agencies, studios, consultancies and freelancers who bill clients by the hour. Time is tracked against a client, project and task, marked billable or not, and turned into invoices at your project or task rates. For that job, a browser tracker on Windows covers what most billing teams need from a desktop app, minus the install.
sections.2.heading: Desktop app or browser: what changes on a Windows PC
sections.2.body:
Here is how a browser-based tracker like Paidlyo compares with a typical installed desktop tracker on Windows:

| | Installed desktop tracker | Paidlyo in a browser |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | Download, install, often needs admin rights | Sign in |
| Updates | Installed on each PC | Nothing to update |
| Using two or more PCs | Install and sign in on each one | Sign in from any browser |
| Company laptops with locked installs | May need IT approval | Usually no approval needed |
| Background app or idle tracking | Often available | Not available |
| Working without internet | Some apps support it | Needs a connection |

If your team moves between an office desktop, a home PC and a laptop, the browser approach removes a lot of small hassles. If you need a tracker that watches activity or works offline, a desktop program is the better fit.

Take a consultant who works on a client's locked-down laptop three days a week, an office PC one day and a home PC on Fridays. With an installed tracker, that's three installs, one of which the client's IT team may refuse. With Paidlyo, it's three sign-ins, and every hour lands in the same timesheet. At month end, the invoice is built from all of them at once, without exporting anything from one machine to another.
sections.3.heading: Making a browser tracker feel like a desktop app
sections.3.body:
A browser tab is easy to lose among twenty others, especially on a busy day. A few simple steps make Paidlyo feel almost like a desktop program on Windows:

1. **Give it its own window.** Open Paidlyo in a separate browser window and keep it on one side of the screen or a second monitor.
2. **Pin it to the taskbar.** Most Windows browsers let you create a shortcut or install a website as an app from the browser menu. It then opens from the taskbar or Start menu like any program.
3. **Pin the tab** if you prefer to keep it in your main window, so it stays at the left and doesn't get closed by accident.
4. **Start the timer when you start the task.** Make it part of opening the file or the ticket.
5. **Fill gaps in the weekly timesheet** at the end of the day, for anything you didn't time.

None of these need admin rights or anything installed from Paidlyo. They use features that are already part of the browser, so they also work on a locked-down company laptop. You can read more about the day-to-day habits in [the Paidlyo timer](/features/timer).
sections.3.callout: Check your day's entries before you shut down the PC. Paidlyo has no idle detection, so a quick review catches a timer left running.
sections.4.heading: Company laptops, shared PCs and IT rules
sections.4.body:
Many companies lock down their Windows laptops so staff can't install software. Contractors and consultants working on a client's machine often face the same rule. A browser-based tracker avoids that problem: if you can open a website, you can track time.

A few practical points for teams:

- **Use your own sign-in on shared PCs,** and sign out when you're done, as you would with any online account.
- **Keep work hours in one account.** Because everything is online, hours tracked on the office PC and the laptop appear in the same timesheet and reports.
- **Give people the right role.** Paidlyo has owner, admin and member roles, so decide who handles billing before you invite the team.
- **Agree how you'll handle no connection.** If someone works on a train or a site without internet, they note their hours and add them to the weekly timesheet later.

For teams spread across locations, there's more on working from any browser in [online time tracking](/time-tracking/online).
sections.5.heading: Who should choose a desktop tracker instead
sections.5.body:
Paidlyo isn't the right Windows time tracker for everyone. Choose an installed desktop program if:

- **You need automatic tracking** of the apps and websites you use, so you don't have to start a timer.
- **You need idle detection** that pauses the timer when you step away.
- **You often work offline** for long periods.
- **You want it free.** Some desktop trackers have free versions. Paidlyo has no free plan; it costs $9 per person a month after a 14-day trial.

Choose Paidlyo if you mainly need clean billable hours by client, project and task, invoices built from those hours, and the same data on every PC without installing anything. For the full weekly view, see [weekly timesheets](/features/timesheets).

If you're not sure, try it for a week on the PCs you actually use. Track your normal client work, check the timesheet on Friday, and see whether you missed the background features at all. The 14-day trial is long enough to run a full test and create a first invoice from real hours.
